worked_solution:
We use the formula for the $n$th term of a geometric sequence to determine ${a}_{1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}{r}^{n-1} \\ 324 & ={a}_{1}\cdot {3}^{(4-1)} \\ 324 & =27{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =12\end{aligned}
$$

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}.
$$

In this case, ${a}_{1}=12$ and $r=3.$ Substituting our values into the formula for ${S}_{N}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{12(1-{3}^{N})}{1-3} \\  & =\frac{12(1-{3}^{N})}{(-2)} \\  & =-6(1-{3}^{N}) \\  & =6({3}^{N}-1).\end{aligned}
$$
